overview: AI models are increasingly applied to complex interactive tasks, from game automation to lab robotics.
Companies are tightening AI usage policies amid copyright concerns and ethical debates.
OpenAI and Anthropic face scrutiny over research disclosure and business sustainability.

top.title: GPT-5.6 Sol can beat Factorio on peaceful mode
top.summary: GPT-5.6 Sol, run via a Python game manager, completed a peaceful Factorio playthrough in 13.5 game hours, demonstrating improved autonomous planning but showing late-game scaling limits.

top.title: Anthropic takes steps to block Claude from reverse-engineering video games
top.summary: Anthropic restricted Claude from modding, decompiling, or reverse‑engineering video games, citing copyright risk after AI‑enabled game hacks raised legal and ethical concerns.

top.title: An AI Agent Injected Drugs Into a Live Mouse’s Brain
top.summary: An AI agent linked to a robotic rig performed a brain injection on a live mouse, selecting therapy and coordinates, highlighting potential for AI‑directed lab procedures.

top.title: Sam Altman sympathizes with mathematicians, but says OpenAI’s math onslaught won’t stop
top.summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman acknowledged the disruptive flood of AI‑generated math results, pledging continued releases despite criticism over attribution and communication.

top.title: Anthropic’s business plan: Build God or die trying
top.summary: Anthropic’s S‑1 filing shows massive revenue growth but huge expenses, emphasizing a strategy focused on enterprise AI services while betting on rapid model self‑improvement.

top.title: Apple CEO says the company doesn’t ‘want to ship AI for AI’s sake’
top.summary: Apple CEO John Ternus said the company will use AI selectively, emphasizing product value over releasing AI features for their own sake.
